Package com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.tokens

Class IssuedTokenClaims

java.lang.Object
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.tokens.IssuedTokenClaims
@Component public class IssuedTokenClaims extends Object
The claims this server adds to the tokens it issues, whatever their format, so the self-contained (JWT) access tokens and the reference (opaque) ones carry the same claims: RolesTenantAudienceTokenCustomizer applies it to the JWTs and ReferenceTokenClaimsCustomizer to the claims stored for a reference token (which the introspection endpoint returns).

An access token gets roles, tenant and aud: the roles are the authorities of the user, the tenant comes from the user account, the audiences from the "settings.client.audiences" custom setting of the client. Tokens of the client credentials grant have no user, so they get no roles and no tenant. An ID token gets none of them. Then every JwtClaimsContributor, in order, adds its own claims to the access and ID tokens (it can tell them apart with OAuth2TokenContext.getTokenType()); no other token is touched.
